answer: Sybil pressure is blunted when entry itself is scarce. Let each established identity vouch for only a few newcomers per interval, and make both sides lock collateral that is slashed if the newcomer is later proven a duplicate. When a tide of look-alike accounts tries to enter together, the graph cannot absorb them faster than sponsors will risk their stake. Each accepted edge also emits a pulse of attestations that peers record in a public atlas of sponsor-to-newcomer links, so mutual-vouching clusters are visible and discounted. Influence then follows costly introductions, not free aliases.
